subject: Capacity guardrail: proposed safety-net reservations for EchoHealth pilot
messages:
From: Eve Larson <eve.larson@echohealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: pmo@echohealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot request: short-term reservation + safety net

Hi Mina / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the EchoHealth team is excited to move the pilot forward. We have one ask before we kick off: can Redwood provision a small, temporary reserved pool (safety-net) for our pilot window so we don't lose critical CPS performance during our integration spike?

High-level needs:
- Duration: 2027-01-04 -> 2027-01-31 (3 weeks plus buffer)
- Target capacity: steady 4 x A100-equivalent slots, burst up to 8 for hourly peaks (approx 30k tokens/min)
- Workload: low-latency chat + embeddings for triage flows

We also need an SLA/fallback behavior if the pool is exhausted (can fallback to a compatible quantized variant, or route to hosted tier). Attached is our pilot capacity request and a short traffic forecast.

Eve
Eve Larson
Program Manager, EchoHealth
[attachment: echo_pilot_capacity_request.pdf (pdf)]
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Eve Larson <eve.larson@echohealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request: short-term reservation + safety net

Eve — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic spreadsheet. Looping in Kimberly (policy/product) and Marcus (capacity/ops) so we can give a concrete reservation proposal and the operational constraints.

Initial thoughts / asks from our side:
- We can offer a time-boxed reserved slice for Jan 4–31 with a clear carveout in the Dedicated pool, but we need to lock a burst policy and eviction window to protect platform SLOs.
- Please confirm whether all traffic requires hard low-latency (99th pct < 200ms), or if some background embedding jobs can be batched with relaxed latency (we can compress those into lower-cost execution paths).
- We'll attach a proposed reservation matrix (reserved_slice_matrix_v1.xlsx) with two options (steady 4 with burst to 8; or steady 6 with smaller burst).

Next steps: Kimberly and Marcus — can you review the attached matrix and respond with whether an exception to autoscale floor is needed, and what fallback model variants we should pre-provision?

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
VP, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[attachment: reserved_slice_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Eve Larson <eve.larson@echohealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request: short-term reservation + safety net

Thanks, Mina and Eve. I reviewed the matrix. Product stance and policy considerations below: 

1) Reservation approach (recommended):
- Offer Option B as a recommended compromise: steady 5 slots reserved, burst to 8 for 6-hour windows (pre-declared by the customer). This reduces platform fragmentation and still covers peak needs.

2) Autoscale / policy exception:
- We can grant a one-off autoscale-floor exception for the pilot, but it must be gated: 1) pre-declared burst windows, 2) a 10% soft-eviction backstop if platform-wide pressure exceeds thresholds, 3) required tagging in requests so we can attribute cost.

3) Fallbacks and model variants:
- Pre-provision a quantized-compatible 7B variant as a fallback route with a documented expected latency increase (~30–50ms) and slightly lower quality. That variant must be registered in rollout config.

4) Commercial / billing note:
- For pilot terms we should offer a discounted unit rate on the reserved slice; finance will need a short SOW. HubSpot deal referenced: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Marcus / Ops: can you confirm node types and whether pre-warming will be required to meet the 99th pct target?

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request: short-term reservation + safety net

Quick ops read:

- Node / slot sizing: A100-equivalent slots are fine. If they want 5 steady + bursts to 8, we should allocate in a single contiguous slice to minimize cross-host KV cache cold starts. That implies reserving 6 physical GPUs (oversubscribe with packing) for the window.
- Pre-warming: required for sustained 99th <200ms for chat paths. We'll need a 12–24 hour pre-warm window before Jan 4 and a lightweight canary on Jan 4 morning.
- Eviction policy: agree to Kimberly's 10% soft-eviction; concrete signal will be platform pressure > 85% cluster utilization for the region. We will add an automatic fallback routing rule to the quantized 7B variant so requests gracefully route if eviction triggers.
- Operational handoff: we need an oncall brief and a runbook snippet (private) that lists rollback, scaling actions, and who to notify. Laura — can you own the runbook and the Doc link?

I'll attach a short ops checklist; if everyone is aligned I'll open the reservation ticket with infra and schedule pre-warm.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Capacity Engineering
Redwood Inference
[attachment: ops_reservation_checklist.md (md)]
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 09:31:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request: short-term reservation + safety net

Thanks all — this looks good. Eve / EchoHealth: summary of agreed items below, feel free to correct: 

- Reservation: Option B (steady 5 slots, burst to 8 for declared windows).
- Dates: Jan 4–31, 2027 with 24h pre-warm Jan 3.
- Policy: 10% soft-eviction threshold; automatic fallback to quantized 7B variant if eviction triggers.
- Ops: Marcus to open infra ticket and own pre-warm; Laura to publish runbook snippet; Kimberly to own billing/SOW.
- Deliverables: reserved_slice_matrix_v1.xlsx (attached), ops checklist attached, HubSpot deal updated (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890).

Action items:
- Eve: confirm the declared hourly burst windows by Dec 20 so we can lock scheduling.
- Kimberly: please coordinate SOW and discount terms.
- Marcus/Laura: please confirm infra ticket number and runbook link by Dec 17.

I'll draft the reservation SOW once we have the burst windows and ticket ID.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
VP, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
